Regulation 5.11 of the CERC GNA Regulations governs the conversion of entities with solar-based connectivity to 'solar hour access' status and provides a mechanism for applying for additional non-solar hour access capacity [1].

Regulation 5.11 governs entities with 'Solar Hour Access' and 'Non-Solar Hour Access' under the GNA Regulations [2]. - First Proviso: The entity has the right to apply for additional capacity under Regulation 5.2 or 5.11(a) within three months of the Regulation's effectiveness, and the Nodal Agency must consider such application during conversion [2].
- Second Proviso: This proviso is mandatory and restricts the conversion of solar connectivity of less than 50 MW, affecting the available margin for non-solar hour access [3] [4].

Applications under Regulation 5.11(a) are considered 'subject to availability of bay and/or margin for such non-solar hour access' [5]. Mere submission of an application or publication of margin details does not create a vested right to a particular quantum of non-solar hour access [6] [7].

| Document | Cure Period | Provision |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Share Purchase Agreement (SPA) | 15 days | Clause 12.3 — Termination for Material Breach | [1]
| CTO Employment Agreement | 15 days | Section 8 — Termination | [2]

Under the Share Purchase Agreement, a party may terminate if the other party commits a material breach "which, if capable of remedy, remains uncured for a period of fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice specifying the breach and requiring it to be remedied" [1].

results.query: Summarise CTUIL's arguments in the reply in Petition 310/MP/2026.
results.answer:
## Summary of CTUIL's Arguments in Reply (Petition 310/MP/2026)

### Preliminary Objection: Petition is Premature and Not Maintainable

CTUIL argues that Petitioner No. 1 (AMPIN Energy Utility Nine Pvt. Ltd.), being merely an applicant with no accrued or vested right, cannot seek an entitlement before its application is processed [1]. Under Regulation 5.11(a), an applicant does not acquire any vested right to a particular quantum of non-solar hour access merely by submitting an application or relying on published margin details [2]. The petition seeks a declaration at the application stage itself that the available margin is 199.5 MW, which CTUIL contends is premature [3].

### The Published Margin Details Were Provisional and Indicative

CTUIL emphasises that the "Details of margins" published on 10.10.2025 was expressly provisional [4]. The document itself stated that "the margins are indicative in nature and the connectivity for solar/non-solar hour access shall be granted as per the detailed system studies after receipt of the application" [5]. CTUIL argues no vested right can be founded on a document that describes its contents as indicative, with actual grant subject to subsequent detailed system studies [6].

### Application of the Second Proviso to Regulation 5.11(b): Margin is 166 MW, Not 199.5 MW

CTUIL applies the Second Proviso to Regulation 5.11(b), which provides that if the quantum of connectivity that can be made available for non-solar hours is less than 50 MW, the entity shall not be converted to solar hour access and shall continue with full day access [7].

Applying this to AEGPL's three connectivity grants at Fatehgarh-IV PS [8]:

1. Application No. 1200003416 (130 MW): Non-solar (wind) component is 44.1 MW; balance available for non-solar hour access is 85.9 MW (exceeds 50 MW threshold) — 85.9 MW available [9].

2. Application No. 0412100019 (120 MW): Non-solar (wind) component is 39.9 MW; balance available is 80.1 MW (exceeds 50 MW threshold) — 80.1 MW available [10].

3. Application No. 0312100007 (50 MW): Non-solar (wind) component is 16.5 MW; balance would be only 33.5 MW, which is less than the 50 MW threshold [11]. Under the Second Proviso, AEGPL continues as an entity with full day access over the entirety of this 50 MW grant — NIL available [12].

Accordingly, the total margin available for non-solar hour access is 85.9 MW + 80.1 MW + Nil = 166 MW, as reflected in the Agenda for the 47th CMETS-NR and the minutes dated 20.07.2026 [13]. CTUIL states the earlier figure of 199.5 MW inadvertently reflected 33.5 MW from Application No. 0312100007 without considering the Second Proviso, and the correction to 166 MW was mandatory under the GNA Regulations [14].

### No Legitimate Expectation Against Statutory Provisions

CTUIL argues that no legitimate expectation can arise from a representation that was itself erroneous and contrary to the express and mandatory terms of the GNA Regulations [15]. It is well-settled that there can be no estoppel or legitimate expectation against the express provisions of a statute or statutory regulation [16]. The Petitioners cannot rely on Regulation 5.11(b) for AEGPL's conversion while resisting the application of the very proviso that restricts conversion where the balance is less than 50 MW [17].

### Petitioner's Hardship is Self-Created

CTUIL contends that Petitioner No. 1 chose to participate in SECI's competitive bidding and accepted the Letter of Award dated 10.02.2026 on the basis of provisional indicative data, without awaiting final grant of its application or confirmation from CTUIL [18]. Any commercial risk flowing from that choice is of the Petitioner's own making and cannot be treated as a "hardship" under Regulation 42 [19].

### Interim Relief Cannot Be Granted

CTUIL submits that the interim reliefs sought, including an ex-parte ad-interim direction restraining CTUIL from allocating third-party rights over the non-solar hour access capacity at Bay No. 212, cannot be sustained as they would be contrary to the specific provisions of the GNA Regulations [20].

### Conclusion

CTUIL denies that the revision of margin from 199.5 MW to 166 MW was arbitrary, characterising it as a bona fide and mandatory correction upon scrutiny of AEGPL's connectivity position [21]. CTUIL prays that the petition be dismissed as not maintainable and devoid of merit [22].

results.query: Why does PSPCL say Regulation 23 of the RE Tariff Regulations 2012 does not apply?
results.answer:
PSPCL advances two principal reasons why Regulation 23 of the RE Tariff Regulations 2012 does not apply [1].

First, the Regulations' scope is limited to Section 62 tariffs. Regulation 3 expressly limits the applicability of the RE Tariff Regulations 2012 to tariffs determined by the Commission under Section 62 of the Electricity Act, 2003 [2]. The Petitioner's tariff of Rs. 7.45/kWh was discovered through competitive bidding under Section 63 and adopted by the Commission's Order dated 11.05.2015, not determined under Section 62 [3]. The Commission had clarified in Petition No. 35 of 2012 that where tariff is discovered through competitive bidding, the RE Tariff Regulations operate only as a benchmark and not as the governing tariff framework [4].

Second, the contractual terms cannot be rewritten. The PPA contains an entire agreement clause and no Change in Law clause [5]. PSPCL contends that clear contractual terms cannot be overridden by importing general regulatory principles like Regulation 23 [6].

units.text: The Petitioner's tariff of Rs. 7.45/kWh was discovered through competitive bidding under Section 63 and adopted by the Commission's Order dated 11.05.2015, not determined under Section 62 [3].

units.text: The Commission had clarified in Petition No. 35 of 2012 that where tariff is discovered through competitive bidding, the RE Tariff Regulations operate only as a benchmark and not as the governing tariff framework [4].
evidence: WRITTEN SUBMISSION IN PETITION NO. 22 OF 2026 (VECTOR GREEN) 01.08.2026.pdf: "Consistent with Regulation 3 [ Page 50, Petition ] of the RE Tariff Regulations, 2012, this Hon'ble Commission, while determing the generic tariff for FY 2012-13 vide Order dated 19.07.2012 [Pages 110-137, Petition] in Petition No. 35 of 2012, clarified that where tariff is discovered through competitive bidding, the RE Tariff Regulations operate only as a benchmark and not as the governing tariff framework [Para 5 at Page 117, Petition ]."

units.text: Second, the contractual terms cannot be rewritten.
